data.current_summary: What a patent cites, and who cites it
data.current_description: Answers: what prior art is on this patent's front page, and which later patents cite it. `backward` is the front-page list grouped by what was cited — `patents` (US, canonical numbers), `publications` (US pre-grant, US20130157853A1), `foreign` (country + number as printed), `npl` (non-patent literature text) — each with `category` (examiner | applicant | other, with `category_detail` for other) and the cited document's `date` at the precision USPTO prints (usually a month), plus `count` / `examiner_count` / `applicant_count`. `forward` is every loaded grant citing this patent number, newest number first: [{patent_number, grant_date, title, categories}] with `count` (distinct citing grants) and `next_cursor` (famous patents have thousands; page with `limit`/`cursor`). A reference USPTO printed unreadably is kept verbatim with a `defect` note. `direction` = both | backward | forward. Coverage is the weekly grant files loaded: a `forward.count` is complete for those weeks only, and `backward` is null with `detail` naming the covered dates when the patent's own grant file is not loaded. Citations of the patent's pre-grant publication are not folded in. Costs 1 request per 100 citation rows returned.

data.current_summary: Office actions (examiner rejections) of one application, with text
data.current_description: Answers: what did the examiner reject, under which statutes, and when is a response due. Each item is one office action (non-final, final, restriction, ...) with mailed_date, the reply deadline per 37 CFR 1.134 / MPEP 710.02(b) (`response_due_estimate`, `response_due_max` with extensions under 1.136(a), `response_period_months`, `response_extendable`, `restarts_period` — all null for an action whose period is set in the letter; on a notice of allowance the estimate is the issue-fee due date), `statutes` and `rejections` when USPTO's parsed data exists — `statutes` carries the bare section beside any paragraphed form (103, 112, 112(a)) so a filter on '103' never misses, and is null rather than empty when USPTO sent no structured rejections at all, which is not the same as an action that rejected nothing. The examiner's prose — `body_text` and the per-statute rejection text inside `sections` — costs include_text=true (tens of KB each); without it `text_chars` and `section_chars` say how much there is to ask for. Text lags mailing by 0–7 days; a transaction can exist before its text does.
data.summary_suggestion: Retrieve office actions with rejection details and response deadlines
data.description_suggestion: Retrieves all office actions for an application, including examiner rejections, applicable statutes, and response deadlines. Each office action contains: mailed_date, response deadline information (response_due_estimate, response_due_max, response_period_months, response_extendable, restarts_period), statutes (bare section numbers like 103, 112, 112(a)), and rejections when USPTO parsed data exists. Optional parameter `include_text=true` retrieves full examiner prose (body_text and per-statute rejection text), which may lag mailing by 0–7 days; without it, text_chars and section_chars indicate available text size. Results ordered newest first. Note: statutes is null when no structured rejections exist, distinct from actions with no rejections.
